| ISC-6..7 | plan | plan section present with steps+verification | complete | Read of final report |
| ISC-8..13 | evidence | counts from audit log / Resend API quoted | numbers or explicit unknown | Agent(Fable) Bash/psql/curl |
| ISC-14..19 | design | queue design section covers budget, priority, backlog | all named elements present | Read of final report |
| ISC-20..22 | evidence | template source + sent wording quoted | verbatim quote present | Agent(Fable) Grep/SQL |
| ISC-23..28 | artefact | drafts present in report, standards applied | branding + context present | Read of final report |
| ISC-29 | analysis | causal chain section with supporting timestamps | confirmed/refuted stated | RootCauseAnalysis |
| ISC-30..31 | report | ordering + sourcing check on final text | pass | ReReadCheck |
| ISC-32 | anti | `git status --porcelain` in code/ empty | empty | Bash |
| ISC-33 | anti | no send/mutation commands in transcript | zero | self-audit |
| ISC-34 | anti | unknowns explicitly marked | zero fabricated numbers | ReReadCheck |

## Features

| name | description | satisfies | depends_on | parallelizable |
|------|-------------|-----------|------------|----------------|
| login-investigation | Agent sweep of auth flow, session config, email dependency | ISC-1..5 | — | true |
| email-audit | Agent sweep of send pipeline, audit log, Resend usage, blast job | ISC-8..13 | — | true |
| template-forensics | Agent sweep of fob-expiry template, sent copy, recipients | ISC-20..22, ISC-25 | — | true |
| causal-chain | RootCauseAnalysis linking the three issues | ISC-29 | login-investigation, email-audit | false |
| queue-design | Daily-budget queue proposal with 15/day auth reserve | ISC-14..19 | email-audit | false |
| drafts | Corrected template copy + one-off correction email | ISC-23..28 | template-forensics | false |
| report | Assemble three-part report with ordered plans | ISC-6..7, ISC-30..31 | all | false |

## Decisions

- 2026-08-01: Task ISA (not project ISA) — this is an incident investigation; durable learnings reconcile to the project later. Delegation: 3 read-only background agents on Fable per Nick's instruction.

---
task: Investigate three AccessBuddy incidents and deliver a report plus action plan per issue
slug: accessbuddy-incident-triage
effort: E3
phase: observe
progress: 0/34
mode: standard
started: 2026-08-01T00:00:00+10:00
updated: 2026-08-01T00:00:00+10:00
---

## Problem

Three linked production incidents at AccessBuddy (SMLSC tenant live): (1) a member reports being logged out and unable to log back in; (2) the Resend daily email limit (100/day free tier) was hit, so an unknown subset of outbound emails silently failed and future blasts risk the same; (3) a fob-expiry notification went out without the critical renewal context ("expires 1 Sep unless you renew; ignore if already renewed"), generating confused member queries. Nick needs evidence-backed diagnosis and a plan per issue before anything is changed.

## Vision

Nick opens one report and instantly sees what actually happened across all three issues — including whether the email limit caused the login failure — with a concrete, low-risk plan per issue he can approve line by line. Nothing has been touched; everything is ready to execute on approval.

## Out of Scope

No code changes, no deploys, no database writes, no emails sent, no template edits — this run is investigation and planning only. No redesign of the wider notification system beyond the queue needed for the daily limit. No Resend plan upgrade decision (surfaced as an option only).

## Constraints

- Read-only against production: SELECTs and API GETs only; no mutations.
- All agent work on the Fable model per Nick's explicit instruction.
- Email architecture facts from `context/facts.md` are authoritative (Resend, 27-event registry, `email_configurations` overrides, `setEmailBranding()` convention).
- Correction email and template copy must carry tenant branding and the renewal business context.
- Plans must respect the existing stack (Bun/Hono, Postgres/Drizzle, Cloud Run) — no new infrastructure unless unavoidable.

## Goal

Deliver a three-part incident report — login failure, email-limit audit with queued-send design (15/day reserved for auth), fob-expiry template fix with correction-email draft and recipient list — each with root cause evidence and an approval-ready action plan, with zero production mutations performed.

## Criteria

### Issue 1 — Login failure
- [ ] ISC-1: Login/auth flow identified with file references (Firebase Auth usage, session lifecycle)
- [ ] ISC-2: Determination whether login depends on outbound email (verification, magic link, password reset)
- [ ] ISC-3: Evidence gathered on whether login-related emails failed during the limit window
- [ ] ISC-4: Any recent deploy/session-config change in the incident window identified or ruled out
- [ ] ISC-5: Root cause stated with confidence level, or explicit open questions listed
- [ ] ISC-6: Action plan for issue 1 with steps, owner, and verification method
- [ ] ISC-7: Immediate unblock path for the affected member named in the plan

### Issue 2 — Email limit audit + queue design
- [ ] ISC-8: Email provider and exact limit confirmed from code/config (Resend tier, 100/day)
- [ ] ISC-9: Sent emails in the incident window enumerated (source: audit log and/or Resend API)
- [ ] ISC-10: Failed/unsent emails enumerated with recipient and event type
- [ ] ISC-11: Failure mode identified (error handling path when limit hit — silent vs logged)
- [ ] ISC-12: The batch job / trigger that caused the blast identified with file reference
- [ ] ISC-13: Total pending sends quantified against the 100/day cap
- [ ] ISC-14: Queue design proposed: persistent queue, daily budget, priority classes
- [ ] ISC-15: Design reserves ~15/day headroom for auth/transactional email
- [ ] ISC-16: Design spreads bulk sends across days with deterministic drain order
- [ ] ISC-17: Design covers retry of the currently-unsent backlog
- [ ] ISC-18: Design names concrete implementation surface (tables, job, code touchpoints)
- [ ] ISC-19: Resend paid-tier upgrade surfaced as costed alternative/complement

### Issue 3 — Fob-expiry template + correction
- [ ] ISC-20: Offending template located (event key, code default vs tenant override) with file/row reference
- [ ] ISC-21: Actual sent wording captured as evidence
- [ ] ISC-22: Why the business context was missing explained (authoring gap vs wrong template path)
- [ ] ISC-23: Corrected template copy drafted (expires 1 Sep, renew to keep access, ignore if renewed)
- [ ] ISC-24: Corrected copy follows email standards (tenant branding, first-name greeting)
- [ ] ISC-25: Recipient list of the bad email produced with count and source evidence
- [ ] ISC-26: One-off correction email drafted for those recipients
- [ ] ISC-27: Correction send plan respects the daily cap and queue design
- [ ] ISC-28: Plan marks correction as once-off (no recurring artefact left behind)

### Cross-cutting
- [ ] ISC-29: Cross-issue causal chain (blast → limit → login) confirmed or refuted with evidence
- [ ] ISC-30: Report orders actions by urgency across all three issues
- [ ] ISC-31: Every claim in the report traceable to a tool-verified source (file, query, API response)
- [ ] ISC-32: Anti: no file under `code/` modified during this run (git status clean)
- [ ] ISC-33: Anti: no email sent and no production row inserted/updated/deleted during this run
- [ ] ISC-34: Anti: report contains no fabricated counts — any unknown is marked unknown

## Test Strategy

| isc | type | check | threshold | tool |
|-----|------|-------|-----------|------|
| ISC-1..5 | evidence | agent report cites files/queries | every claim sourced | Agent(Fable) + Read |
| ISC-6..7 | plan | plan section present with steps+verification | complete | Read of final report |
| ISC-8..13 | evidence | counts from audit log / Resend API quoted | numbers or explicit unknown | Agent(Fable) Bash/psql/curl |
| ISC-14..19 | design | queue design section covers budget, priority, backlog | all named elements present | Read of final report |
| ISC-20..22 | evidence | template source + sent wording quoted | verbatim quote present | Agent(Fable) Grep/SQL |
| ISC-23..28 | artefact | drafts present in report, standards applied | branding + context present | Read of final report |
| ISC-29 | analysis | causal chain section with supporting timestamps | confirmed/refuted stated | RootCauseAnalysis |
| ISC-30..31 | report | ordering + sourcing check on final text | pass | ReReadCheck |
| ISC-32 | anti | `git status --porcelain` in code/ empty | empty | Bash |
| ISC-33 | anti | no send/mutation commands in transcript | zero | self-audit |
| ISC-34 | anti | unknowns explicitly marked | zero fabricated numbers | ReReadCheck |

## Features

| name | description | satisfies | depends_on | parallelizable |
|------|-------------|-----------|------------|----------------|
| login-investigation | Agent sweep of auth flow, session config, email dependency | ISC-1..5 | — | true |
| email-audit | Agent sweep of send pipeline, audit log, Resend usage, blast job | ISC-8..13 | — | true |
| template-forensics | Agent sweep of fob-expiry template, sent copy, recipients | ISC-20..22, ISC-25 | — | true |
| causal-chain | RootCauseAnalysis linking the three issues | ISC-29 | login-investigation, email-audit | false |
| queue-design | Daily-budget queue proposal with 15/day auth reserve | ISC-14..19 | email-audit | false |
| drafts | Corrected template copy + one-off correction email | ISC-23..28 | template-forensics | false |
| report | Assemble three-part report with ordered plans | ISC-6..7, ISC-30..31 | all | false |

## Decisions

- 2026-08-01: Task ISA (not project ISA) — this is an incident investigation; durable learnings reconcile to the project later. Delegation: 3 read-only background agents on Fable per Nick's instruction.

<result># AccessBuddy QA — Login Outage Investigation (read-only)

Per instruction I modified nothing (memory.md update deferred; noted below). All paths under `/home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/code/`.

---

## FLOW

Login is **NOT** password-based. Three paths, all landing on a `session` cookie with a **14-day** lifetime:

1. **Browser (default): Firebase magic link via Resend.** `apps/web/src/app/sign-in/sign-in-form.tsx:85-97` — non-PWA posts to `/api/auth/send-magic-link`. `apps/web/src/lib/services/magic-link.ts:36-39` generates the link via `adminAuth.generateSignInWithEmailLink(...)` and sends it with `sendTemplatedEmail(email, "magicLink", ...)` (lines 54-78). Callback exchanges the Firebase ID token at `/api/auth/session` for a Firebase session cookie: `apps/web/src/app/api/auth/session/route.ts:6` — `const SESSION_MAX_AGE = 60 * 60 * 24 * 14; // 14 days`.

2. **PWA / installed app: email OTP.** `sign-in-form.tsx:75-84` — standalone mode posts to `/api/auth/send-otp`. That route sends template key **`verificationCode`**: `apps/web/src/app/api/auth/send-otp/route.ts:96-109` (`sendTemplatedEmail(email, "verificationCode", { code }, ...)`). Subject rendered at `apps/web/src/lib/services/email.ts:676`: `` `Your ${clubName} verification code` ``. Code is 6-digit, hashed in Postgres `otp_codes`, TTL 5 min, 5 attempts (`apps/web/src/lib/otp-store.ts:19-20`). Verify route mints an HMAC-signed `webauthn.*` cookie: `apps/web/src/app/api/auth/verify-otp/route.ts:72-81`, `maxAge: SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` = 14 days (`apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:9`).

3. **Passkey (WebAuthn / Face ID)** — only offered if `localStorage.getItem("passkey_prompted") === "true"` (`sign-in-form.tsx:38-40`), i.e. only previously-enrolled devices. Mints the same signed cookie (`apps/web/src/app/api/auth/webauthn/login/route.ts:127-138`). **No email involved.**

**What logs a user out:** (a) 14-day cookie expiry; (b) for OTP/passkey sessions, any change to `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET` — verification is unconditional and fail-closed (`auth.ts:59-93`); (c) `DELETE /api/auth/session`.

## ERROR-PATH — Resend cap exhausted (hypothesis CONFIRMED in code)

**A Resend failure is fully swallowed; the user is told the email was sent.**

`apps/web/src/lib/services/email.ts:224-249` — `sendEmail` on Resend API error:

```ts
if (result.error) {
  console.error(`[email] Failed to send "${subject}" to ${to}:`, result.error);
  if (audit) {
    await writeEmailAudit(audit, { success: false, ... error: String(result.error.message ?? result.error) });
  }
  return;   // <-- returns void. Never throws.
}
```

A daily-quota 429 from Resend arrives as `result.error` (the SDK does not throw), so:

- **OTP path:** `send-otp/route.ts:96-122` — `await sendTemplatedEmail(...)` resolves normally, route falls through to `return NextResponse.json({ sent: true })`. UI then shows "We sent a 6-digit code to {email}" (`sign-in-form.tsx:205-207`). The member waits for a code that never arrives. The OTP row IS written first (`route.ts:56`), so a valid code exists in the DB — but nobody can read it (scrypt-hashed, `otp-store.ts:41`).
- **Magic-link path:** identical swallow — `magic-link.ts` → `sendTemplatedEmail` → `sendEmail` returns void; route returns `{ sent: true }` (`send-magic-link/route.ts:95`). Note `magic-link.ts:26-27` deliberately bypasses the tenant `sendEmails` flag ("auth-critical") but has no protection against Resend itself refusing.
- **It IS logged:** `email.ts:239-247` writes an `email_failed` audit entry (action `AuditAction.EMAIL_FAILED`, metadata includes `error`) — via `writeEmailAudit` (`email.ts:276-315`) — and a `console.error` line `[email] Failed to send ...` reaches Cloud Run stdout. It surfaces to the user **never**.

So: **Resend cap exhausted ⇒ both email login methods return success to the UI while silently failing.** Only passkey login still works.

## EVIDENCE

What I could and could not verify from this box:

- **Resend API probe (tried):** the only key available locally (`code/.env:20`) is restricted — `GET /domains` and `GET /emails` both returned `{"statusCode":401,"message":"This API key is restricted to only send emails","name":"restricted_api_key"}`. No quota/delivery data obtainable. Whether this key is the same Resend account as prod is UNVERIFIED (prod key lives in Secret Manager per `.env.prod.template:35`).
- **Prod DB (tried, unavailable):** local `.env:2` points at `localhost:5432` (dev). Prod `DATABASE_URL` is Cloud SQL private IP via Secret Manager (`.env.prod.template:12`). **`gcloud` is not installed on this box** (`command not found`), so no Secret Manager read, no Cloud SQL proxy, no Cloud Run log read. `gh` also not installed.

content.text:
The login investigation agent has reported back — the hypothesis held, and it found two compounding causes:

1. **Why members got logged out:** the 14 July v1.11.0 deploy included `fix(auth): remove Host-header trust and fail closed on session signing`, which replaced the session-signing key — every existing OTP/passkey session cookie instantly failed verification. Anyone who re-signed-in around the deploy also hit natural 14-day cookie expiry around 28 July. Both land in the incident window.
2. **Why they can't log back in:** login is email-only (Firebase magic link in browser, 6-digit OTP in the PWA). The fob-expiry cron (`api/cron/daily/route.ts`) fires 30-day warnings for the SMLSC cohort whose credentials all expire 1 September — that's up to 354 credentials, right now, which blew Resend's 100/day free-tier cap. Critically, `sendEmail` **swallows** the Resend error and returns void, so the sign-in routes still return `{ sent: true }` and the UI says "check your email" while nothing was delivered. The member is stuck in a silent loop, and each retry invalidates the previous undelivered code.

It also flagged forward risk: tomorrow's cron tranche will re-exhaust the cap, and the 7-day warning wave around 25 August will do it again. Failures ARE logged (`email_failed` audit rows plus Cloud Run stderr), so the sent-vs-failed audit is recoverable — but this box lacks `gcloud` and prod DB credentials, so the agent supplied the exact read-only queries to run instead of numbers. The local Resend key is send-only (401 on read endpoints), so Resend-side logs need the dashboard.

Two agents still running (email audit, template forensics). I'll hold synthesis until they report.

<result># Fob-Expiry Email Blast — Investigation Findings

Read-only investigation, all evidence tool-verified. No files modified (the READ-ONLY constraint also blocked my usual memory.md update; carry these findings forward manually if wanted).

## PROVIDER-LIMITS

**Provider: Resend, via the official SDK.** `/home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/code/apps/web/src/lib/services/email.ts:2` (`import { Resend } from "resend"`), instantiated lazily at `email.ts:62-68` from `RESEND_API_KEY`. If the key is unset, sends silently no-op (`email.ts:206-219`, audit entry written with `noop: true`).

**Key locations:**
- Local dev: `code/.env:20` — `RESEND_API_KEY=re_GvmoL2Rh_...`
- Prod: Secret Manager secret `resend-api-key`, wired into Cloud Run at `code/infra/terraform/main.tf:371-378`; the value also sits in the local `code/infra/terraform/prod.tfvars` (`resend_api_key` line present, 1 match). `.env.prod.template:35` confirms: `RESEND_API_KEY=re_... # Secret Manager: resend-api-key`.
- **Both keys are send-only restricted.** Verified live: `GET https://api.resend.com/emails` with each key returns `{"statusCode":401,"message":"This API key is restricted to only send emails","name":"restricted_api_key"}`. Good security posture, but it closes the Resend-API evidence path.

**Plan limits:** Resend's public pricing page (fetched today) confirms the free tier is **100 emails/day, 3,000 emails/month**. The actual 429/limit error text from the incident is **UNVERIFIED** — I could not reach Cloud Logging, the prod DB, or the Resend list API (see ACCESS-NOTES). The exact error string will be in `audit_log.metadata->>'error'` on the `email_failed` rows and in the `[email] Failed to send` console lines.

Note: the same key also serves magic-link sign-in emails, OTP codes, the contact form, and all 27 workflow events — all count toward the same 100/day.

## BLAST-SOURCE

**Trigger: Cloud Scheduler → the daily cron route.** Terraform at `main.tf:469-492`:
```hcl
resource "google_cloud_scheduler_job" "daily_cron" {
  name        = "accessbuddy-daily-cron"
  schedule    = "0 2 * * *" # 2am AEST daily
  time_zone   = "Australia/Melbourne"
  http_target { http_method = "GET"
    uri = ".../api/cron/daily"
    headers = { "x-cron-secret" = var.cron_secret } }
  retry_config { retry_count = 3 ... }
```
Handler: `code/apps/web/src/app/api/cron/daily/route.ts`. Two expiry-email paths, both sending to the credential owner's `users.email`:

1. **Expiry warnings (the likely blast)** — `route.ts:374-403`. Selection: active credentials with an `expiresAt` within the next 31 days:
```ts
.where(and(
  eq(credentials.status, CredentialStatus.ACTIVE),
  isNotNull(credentials.expiresAt),
  lt(credentials.expiresAt, new Date(now.getTime() + 31 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)),
  gte(credentials.expiresAt, now)
))
```
then filtered to exactly 30 or 7 days out (`route.ts:401-403`): `if (diffDays !== 30 && diffDays !== 7) continue;`. Template `credentialExpiryWarning`, subject **"ACTION REQUIRED: Your credential is expiring soon"** (`email.ts:631-637`).

2. **Expired-credential emails** — `route.ts:214-294`. Selection: ALL active credentials with `expiresAt < now`, each flipped to EXPIRED and emailed (`credentialExpired`, "Your credential has expired").

These are the only three files touching `credentialExpiryWarning`/`credentialExpired` (`email-templates.ts`, `email.ts`, `cron/daily/route.ts`) — no manual admin path; the blast was the scheduler.

**Why now:** the platform's expiry convention is 1 September season end — `route.ts:150`: `newExpiry = month >= 6 ? new Date(year + 1, 8, 1) : new Date(year, 8, 1)`. 30 days before 1 Sep 2026 lands 1-2 Aug — exactly the incident window. A seasonal cohort sharing a 1 Sep expiry all satisfy `diffDays === 30` in a single run.

## SENT-VS-FAILED

**UNKNOWN — no reachable source from this machine.** Do not trust any count until one of these runs:

**(a) Prod DB audit log (best source).** Cloud SQL `accessbuddy-production` is private-IP only (`main.tf:132-133`: `ipv4_enabled = false`), so it needs cloud-sql-proxy + gcloud auth (neither installed here). `audit_log` is FORCE RLS (`packages/db/drizzle/0001_rls_policies.sql:52,86`) — connect as `postgres` (superuser bypasses RLS) or run `SELECT set_config('app.current_tenant_id','<smlsc-uuid>', false);` first.
```bash
gcloud auth login
cloud-sql-proxy accessbuddy-prod:australia-southeast1:accessbuddy-production --port 5433
psql "host=127.0.0.1 port=5433 dbname=accessbuddy user=postgres"
```
```sql
-- Totals + per-event-type breakdown, incident window
SELECT action, metadata->>'templateType' AS template, count(*)
FROM audit_log
WHERE action IN ('email_sent','email_failed')
  AND created_at >= now() - interval '4 days'
  AND coalesce(metadata->>'suppressed','') <> 'true'   -- tenant opt-out, not a real send
  AND coalesce(metadata->>'noop','') <> 'true'          -- key unset, not a real send
GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;

-- Recipient list of FAILED sends, with the actual Resend error text
SELECT created_at, metadata->>'to' AS recipient, metadata->>'subject' AS subject,
       metadata->>'templateType' AS template, metadata->>'error' AS error
FROM audit_log
WHERE action = 'email_failed' AND created_at >= now() - interval '4 days'
ORDER BY created_at;
```

**(b) Resend API:** blocked by the restricted key. Requires creating a full-access key in the Resend dashboard, then `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.resend.com/emails?limit=100"`.

**(c) Cloud Logging:** `gcloud` not installed (Linux box or `ssh mac`). Once available:
```bash
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND resource.labels.service_name="accessbuddy-production" AND (textPayload:"[email] Failed to send" OR textPayload:"Cron daily completed")' --project=accessbuddy-prod --freshness=96h --format='value(timestamp,textPayload)' --limit=1000
```
The `Cron daily completed: {...}` line (`route.ts:575`) logs per-run counts (`expiryWarnings`, `expiredCredentialEmails`, `paymentReminders`, `pickupReminders`, `dailySummaryRecipients`) — but note those counters increment even on failed sends (sendEmail never throws), so they are **attempted**, not delivered. Only the audit log distinguishes sent vs failed.

## FAILURE-MODE

**Fire-and-forget. No retry, no queue, error logged + audited, then swallowed.** `email.ts:223-273`:
```ts
const result = await resend.emails.send({ from, replyTo, to, subject, html, ... });
if (result.error) {
  console.error(`[email] Failed to send "${subject}" to ${to}:`, result.error);
  if (audit) { await writeEmailAudit(audit, { success: false, ... error: String(result.error.message ?? result.error) }); }
  return;   // <- no retry, no rethrow
}
```
The catch branch (`email.ts:261-273`) does the same. Consequences, all code-verified:

1. **The loop keeps burning through recipients after the cap.** `sendEmail` returns void and never throws, so the cron loops (`route.ts:225-294`, `395-454`) sequentially attempt every remaining recipient; each post-cap send fails and is written as `email_failed`.
2. **No scheduler-level retry either.** The route returns 200 even if every email failed (per-item try/catch at `route.ts:269-287` and `451-453` swallows errors), so Cloud Scheduler's `retry_count = 3` never fires for email failures.
3. **Failed 30-day warnings are permanently lost.** The warning fires only when `diffDays === 30` exactly (`route.ts:403`); the next day the same credential is at 29 days and skips. There is no audit-dedupe/backfill for expiry warnings (unlike `pickupReminder`, which checks recent `email_sent` entries at `route.ts:484-499`). Failed recipients' next automatic touch is the 7-day warning.
4. **The only queue in the system is admin daily-summary notifications** (`email.ts:861-863`, `notifications` table). Member-facing emails have no queue and no backoff.
5. Conversely, if the route DID 500 mid-run and Scheduler retried, expiry warnings would double-send (no dedupe) — fragile in both directions.

## FORWARD-RISK

**Exact counts UNKNOWN** (needs prod DB; migration source xlsx not on this machine — `code/data/` is empty, no csv/xlsx in the repo). Structural assessment:

- Tenant scale: SMLSC, 192 members / **354 credentials** (ISA ISC-6). Expiry convention is 1 September (`route.ts:150`); the SMLSC import took real `Expiry` dates from the source sheet (`packages/db/src/migrate-smlsc.ts:570`), and the legacy status "Active - Expiring" (`migrate-smlsc.ts:136`) implies a large seasonal cohort.
- If the active seasonal cohort shares ~1 Sep 2026, three more single-day spikes are already scheduled: **~25 Aug** (7-day warnings to the same cohort, including everyone who failed this time), **~1-2 Sep** (a `credentialExpired` email to EVERY still-active cohort credential in one run, `route.ts:214-294`), plus normal daily traffic (magic links, summaries, payment/pickup reminders) on top. Any cohort over ~100 hits the cap again; over ~90 is at risk once baseline traffic is added.
- Sizing query (same psql session as above):
```sql
SELECT expires_at::date AS expiry_day, count(*)
FROM credentials
WHERE status = 'active' AND expires_at IS NOT NULL
  AND expires_at < now() + interval '70 days'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
```
If any single `expiry_day` exceeds ~90-100, both the 7-day-warning run and the expiry-day run will breach the free tier again.

## ACCESS-NOTES

| Source | Result |
|---|---|
| Repo at `~/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/code` | Worked — all code/Terraform evidence from here |
| Local `.env` Resend key (`.env:20`) | Present but send-only restricted; `GET /emails` → 401 `restricted_api_key` |
| Prod Resend key in `infra/terraform/prod.tfvars` | Present; also send-only restricted (same 401) |
| `gcloud` (Linux box) | Not installed; no `~/.config/gcloud` |
| `gcloud` (via `ssh mac`) | Mac reachable; `gcloud not found` |
| Prod Cloud SQL | Private IP only (`main.tf:132`); no proxy/psql/creds path from here |
| Local `DATABASE_URL` | `localhost:5432/accessbuddy` — dev DB only, no incident data |
| resend.com/pricing (WebFetch) | Worked — confirmed 100/day, 3,000/month free tier |
| Last repo commit | `a9e3035` 2026-07-14 — no code changed during the incident window |

**Bottom line:** the blast is the 2am `accessbuddy-daily-cron` 30-day expiry-warning pass over a seasonal ~1 Sep expiry cohort; sends past Resend's 100/day free cap failed silently (logged + audited, never retried), the failed cohort will not get their 30-day warning at all, and the same cohort produces two more scheduled spikes (~25 Aug and ~1-2 Sep) that will breach the cap again unless the plan is upgraded or sends are batched/throttled. Definitive sent/failed numbers and the failed-recipient list are one `psql` session away using the queries above.</result>

Migration `packages/db/drizzle/0010_auth_tokens_email_config_indexes.sql:46-52` states: *"this table is declared in packages/db/src/schema/email-config.ts and read/written by the email-template admin route, but NO migration ever created it... The feature therefore 500s in production today with 'relation does not exist'."* Migration 0010 exists only on the unmerged branch `fix/tenant-2-readiness` (commit 76d7d90); prod is v1.10.2 from `main` (`.release-please-manifest.json` = 1.10.2, main HEAD 288ac64 "release 1.10.2"). This matches ISA ISC-9 (unchecked).
3. `git diff main..HEAD` on `email-templates.ts` and `cron/daily/route.ts` is empty — the template I quoted is byte-identical to what main/prod runs.

So the exact member-visible email: subject **"ACTION REQUIRED: Your credential is expiring soon"**, body **"Dear \<First\>, Your credential expires on \<date\>. Please take action to renew it before it expires. Serial: ... Expires: ... Submit a renewal request through AccessBuddy to maintain your access."** The expiry date WAS included (cron passes `expiresAt` formatted en-AU, `daily/route.ts:422-426`); what was missing is the membership context. Prod DB verification query (once connected via cloud-sql-proxy, see RECIPIENTS) to confirm verbatim: the audit metadata stores the full rendered `html` (`email.ts:306`).

## WHY-MISSING

Three compounding causes:

1. **The code default was always this bare.** Introduced in commit `f36375a` (2026-04-01, "feat: close all notification gaps from original Apps Script version", in v1.0.0) with essentially identical wording; the only commit ever to touch it. It talks about renewing "the credential" via AccessBuddy, never mentions membership renewal, the 1 September season boundary, or "ignore if already renewed".
2. **No override existed and none could exist:** the `email_configurations` table is missing in prod (migration never applied), and even where the table exists the send path ignores it — tenant overrides are currently dead configuration for all 27 events.
3. **Latent variable mismatch for the future:** the registry declares the variable key `expiryDate` (`email-events.ts:394`) but the cron and code template use `expiresAt` (`email.ts:450`, `daily/route.ts:435`). The day block-based overrides go live, `{{expiryDate}}` will not be substituted by a send path passing `expiresAt`. Not the cause of this incident, but a booby trap on the fix path.

## SELECTION-LOGIC

The cron does **NOT** exclude renewed members. Evidence chain:

- Selection (`daily/route.ts:376-403`): all `ACTIVE` credentials with `expiresAt` in `[now, now+31d]`, sent when `diffDays === 30 || diffDays === 7`. The query filters on nothing else — no membership renewal status, no `programmingRequired`, no `pendingExpiresAt`.
- Renewal (attestation) completion does NOT move the live expiry: `apps/web/src/app/api/v1/t/[slug]/attestations/[token]/route.ts:199-215` — *"The live expiresAt is NOT updated until a programmer confirms the access control system has been updated"*; it only stages `pendingExpiresAt` and sets `programmingRequired: true`. Promotion happens in `credentials/[id]/confirm-programming/route.ts:69-90`.

**Conclusion: members who had already renewed (completed attestation) but whose fobs had not yet been reprogrammed and confirmed by the programmer received the warning too.** Only members whose renewal was fully processed through to "Confirm Programming" (live `expiresAt` pushed to next season) were excluded. The "ignore if renewed" line is therefore load-bearing, and a code fix should additionally skip credentials where `pendingExpiresAt > now` (renewal already in the pipeline).

## RECIPIENTS

**UNKNOWN from this machine.** Evidence of why: local `.env` `DATABASE_URL` points at `localhost:5432` (dev); `.env.prod.template` uses a `<cloud-sql-private-ip>` placeholder; no `psql`, `gcloud`, or `cloud-sql-proxy` on PATH. The local `RESEND_API_KEY` is send-only restricted — `GET https://api.resend.com/emails` returned `{"statusCode":401,"message":"This API key is restricted to only send emails","name":"restricted_api_key"}`, so listing via Resend is blocked here (the Resend dashboard, or a full-access key, would also work).

Exact prod query (audit metadata stores `to`, `subject`, `templateType`, `resendId` — `email.ts:298-306`). Run against Cloud SQL `accessbuddy` DB in project `accessbuddy-prod` via cloud-sql-proxy; `audit_log` is RLS-forced, so set tenant context first:

```sql
BEGIN;
SELECT set_config('app.current_tenant_id',
       (SELECT id::text FROM tenants WHERE slug = 'smlsc'), true);

SELECT al.created_at,
       al.metadata->>'to'       AS recipient_email,
       u.first_name, u.last_name,
       c.serial_number,
       c.expires_at,
       al.metadata->>'resendId' AS resend_id
FROM audit_log al
LEFT JOIN credentials c ON c.id = al.entity_id
LEFT JOIN users u ON u.id = c.owner_id
WHERE al.action = 'email_sent'
  AND al.metadata->>'templateType' = 'credentialExpiryWarning'
  AND al.created_at >= now() - interval '4 days'
ORDER BY al.created_at;
-- count:
SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log
WHERE action = 'email_sent'
  AND metadata->>'templateType' = 'credentialExpiryWarning'
  AND created_at >= now() - interval '4 days';
COMMIT;
```

Override-presence check (expected to error with `relation "email_configurations" does not exist`, which itself confirms no override):

```sql
SELECT ec.event_id, ec.enabled, ec.subject_override, ec.blocks
FROM email_configurations ec
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = ec.tenant_id
WHERE t.slug = 'smlsc'
  AND ec.event_id IN ('credential_expiry_warning', 'credential_expired');
```

I have not fabricated any names; the join above yields the definitive list.

## DRAFT-CORRECTED-TEMPLATE

For `credentialExpiryWarningEmail` (subject in `email.ts:634`, body in `email-templates.ts:614-636`). `${expiresAt}` renders as e.g. "1 September 2026"; `${firstName}` is the existing `memberName.split(" ")[0]`.

**Subject:** `Your ${clubName} fob will expire on ${expiresAt} unless you renew your membership`

**Body:**

> Hi ${firstName},
>
> Your fob (serial ${serialNumber}) is due to expire on **${expiresAt}**.
>
> Fob access is tied to your club membership. If you renew your membership for the coming season, your fob stays active — its expiry is extended automatically once your renewal is processed, and you do not need to do anything with the fob itself.
>
> **If you have already renewed your membership, you can ignore this email.** Your fob's expiry will be updated shortly.
>
> If you have not renewed yet, please renew your membership before ${expiresAt} to keep your access.
>
> Any questions, just reply to this email.

(Greeting kept "Hi" per Nick's outreach-tone preference; swap to "Dear" if club convention prefers. A renewal URL variable could be added, but that needs a new variable through the cron and registry — keep v1 copy-only to ship fast.)

## DRAFT-CORRECTION-EMAIL

Once-off to the recipient list from the query above:

**Subject:** `About the fob expiry email — what it actually means`

> Hi ${firstName},
>
> In the last few days you received an automated email from AccessBuddy saying your fob is expiring soon. Sorry — it was missing the context, and understandably caused some confusion.
>

Renewing your membership keeps your fob active — once your renewal is processed, the fob's expiry is extended automatically and you do not need to do anything with the fob itself.
>
> **If you have already renewed your membership, there is nothing you need to do** — please ignore both this and the earlier email.
>
> If you have not renewed yet, please renew before 1 September to keep your access.
>
> Apologies again for the confusion. The wording of the automated email has been fixed so future reminders explain this properly.

## FIX-PATH-RECOMMENDATION

**Code default change is the only path that works, and is the right one anyway.**

- An `email_configurations` override row is impossible in prod today (table does not exist; migration 0010 is unmerged) and would be inert even if it existed, because no send path reads that table — overrides are editor-only until the block renderer is wired into `renderTemplate()`.
- The fix is an edit to `credentialExpiryWarningEmail()` in `apps/web/src/lib/email-templates.ts` plus the subject string at `email.ts:634`. Ship as a `fix:` conventional commit on `main` — per the ISA, `fix:` triggers a release-please deploy (a `chore:` would merge without deploying, a known trap).
- Recommend bundling in the same fix: skip warnings for credentials with `pendingExpiresAt` set (renewed, awaiting reprogramming) in `daily/route.ts` section 1e, and review `credentialExpiredEmail` (`email-templates.ts:592-612`), which has the same missing-context problem and fires on 1 September for anyone still unprocessed.

# AccessBuddy Incident Report — Email Cap, Login Failure, Fob-Expiry Template

**Date:** 2026-08-01 · **Status:** DRAFT for Nick's review — no changes executed, nothing sent
**Sources:** three read-only Fable investigation agents (login flow, email pipeline audit, template forensics), file:line evidence throughout. Counts requiring prod DB access are marked UNKNOWN with the exact query to obtain them.

---

## Executive summary

The three reported issues are one incident with one root cause and one independent trigger.

On 1–2 August the 2am daily cron (`accessbuddy-daily-cron` → `/api/cron/daily`) sent 30-day fob-expiry warnings to the SMLSC seasonal cohort. Because the platform normalises season expiry to **1 September**, the entire active cohort (up to 354 credentials) qualified in a single run — far past Resend's free-tier cap of **100 emails/day**. Every send past the cap failed. The failure is swallowed in code (`sendEmail` logs, writes an `email_failed` audit row, returns void), so:

- **Issue 1 (login):** login is email-only (Firebase magic link in browser, 6-digit OTP in PWA). With the cap exhausted, auth emails fail silently while the UI says "we sent you a code". Members were logged out in the first place by the 14 July v1.11.0 deploy (`cd70131` rotated the session-signing key, invalidating all OTP/passkey sessions) and/or natural 14-day cookie expiry ~28 July. Logout was benign; the inability to log back in is the Resend cap.
- **Issue 2 (email limit):** sends past ~100/day failed silently; failed 30-day warnings are **permanently lost** (the warning fires only at exactly 30 days out; no dedupe/backfill). Two more cap-breaching spikes are already scheduled: **~25 Aug** (7-day warnings, same cohort) and **~1–2 Sep** (credential-expired blast).
- **Issue 3 (template):** the bare wording is the hardcoded code default — the per-tenant override system is dead configuration (the `email_configurations` table doesn't exist in prod; no send path reads it anyway). The cron also does **not** exclude members who already renewed (only fully reprogrammed-and-confirmed credentials are excluded), so renewed members legitimately got the warning — hence the confusion.

## Causal chain

```
Season expiry normalised to 1 Sep (route.ts:150)
  → whole cohort hits diffDays === 30 on the same day (1–2 Aug)
    → cron attempts up to ~354 sends in one run
      → Resend free tier caps at 100/day
        → sends 101+ fail; sendEmail swallows error (email.ts:224-249)
          → auth emails (magic link / OTP) also fail silently
            → members logged out by 14 Jul key rotation / cookie expiry cannot re-authenticate
```

Contributing factors: fire-and-forget send path (no queue, no retry, no daily budget); auth and bulk email share one unprioritised quota; template lacked business context since v1.0.0 (`f36375a`); override system unwired; no alerting on `email_failed` bursts.

---

## Issue 1 — Member cannot log in

**Root cause:** logout = session-signing key rotation (14 Jul deploy) or 14-day cookie expiry; blocked re-login = Resend cap + silently swallowed send failure (`email.ts:224-249` returns void; `/api/auth/send-otp` and `/api/auth/send-magic-link` return `{ sent: true }` regardless).

**Evidence:** `apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:9,59-93` (fail-closed HMAC verification, 14-day TTL); `sign-in-form.tsx:75-97` (email-only paths); commit `cd70131`; agents' full traces.

**Plan (in order):**
1. Check the Resend dashboard for quota state; daily reset is midnight UTC = 10:00 AEST.
2. Unblock the member today: passkey login if previously enrolled; otherwise resend OTP/magic link after quota reset; fallback — generate a Firebase sign-in link via Admin SDK and send it from your own mailbox (needs your approval to contact the member).
3. Pause or gate the cron's email sections until the queue/limit fix ships, so tomorrow's run doesn't re-break login.
4. Code fix (with issue 2): propagate send failures for auth-critical templates so sign-in routes return an honest error instead of `{ sent: true }`.
5. Comms: brief reply to the member (and any others who report it) explaining the outage window.

**Verification:** member confirms login; `audit_log` shows no `email_failed` rows for `verificationCode`/`magicLink` after fix.

## Issue 2 — Email cap: what sent, what didn't, and the queue

**What sent vs what didn't:** recoverable but UNKNOWN from this box — prod Cloud SQL is private-IP only, `gcloud` is not installed (Linux box or Mac), and both Resend API keys are send-only restricted (401 on read endpoints). Two paths to the numbers:
- **Fastest:** Resend dashboard → Emails view (or create a temporary full-access API key and `GET /emails`).
- **Authoritative:** one read-only psql session via cloud-sql-proxy; queries prepared (per-template sent/failed counts, failed-recipient list with error text, cohort-sizing by expiry day) — see Appendix A.

**Failure mode:** fire-and-forget; no retry, no queue; cron returns 200 even if every email failed; failed 30-day warnings never re-fire.

**Queue design (proposed):**
- New `email_queue` table (id, tenant, template, recipient, payload, priority, status, attempts, earliest_send_at, created_at, sent_at, error).
- **Priority classes:** P0 auth (magic link, OTP — sent inline, never queued, but counted); P1 transactional (payment, pickup, approval); P2 bulk (expiry warnings, summaries, correction blasts).
- **Daily budget:** cap outbound at **85/day** (100 − 15 reserved for P0 auth). A counter (Postgres, day-keyed) increments on every send including auth; the drain job stops P1/P2 when the counter hits 85, P0 always allowed to 100.
- **Drain:** cron (reuse `/api/cron/daily` or a new 15-min cron) drains queue oldest-first within priority, spreading the ~354-recipient cohort across ~4–5 days automatically.
- **Retry/backlog:** failed sends set `status='failed'` and re-queue with backoff (max 3 attempts); the currently-lost 30-day warnings get backfilled by enqueueing everyone from the failed-recipient query.
- **Cron change:** expiry-warning windows become ranges (e.g. 30–26 days and 7–3 days with sent-dedupe against `email_queue`/audit) so spreading over days doesn't skip anyone.
- **Guardrail:** alert (or at minimum a daily-summary line) when `email_failed` > 0 or queue depth > budget × 2.

**Alternative/complement:** Resend Pro (~US$20/mo, 50k emails/mo, no daily cap) removes the ceiling instantly. **Recommendation: do both** — upgrade now for the September crunch (renewal season traffic: warnings, expired notices, correction email, plus login traffic from confused members all collide this month), keep the queue as structural protection and for per-tenant budgets when tenant 2 lands.

**Verification:** cohort-sizing query shows no single day exceeding budget; simulated 429 produces queued retry, not silent loss.

## Issue 3 — Fob-expiry template + one-off correction

**What actually went out** (hardcoded default, certain — override system unwired and its table absent in prod):
> Subject: "ACTION REQUIRED: Your credential is expiring soon"
> "Dear \<First\>, Your credential expires on \<date\>. Please take action to renew it before it expires. Serial… Expires… Submit a renewal request through AccessBuddy to maintain your access."

The expiry date was present; the membership context was not, and it's been that way since v1.0.0. Renewed-but-not-yet-reprogrammed members were **not** excluded (only confirm-programming completion moves live `expiresAt`), so they received it too.

**Fix path:** edit the code default — `credentialExpiryWarningEmail()` in `apps/web/src/lib/email-templates.ts:614-636` and the subject at `email.ts:634`. Ship as `fix:` (release-please deploys `fix:`, not `chore:`). An override row is impossible (table missing) and would be inert anyway. Bundle in the same commit: skip warnings where `pendingExpiresAt` is set (renewal in pipeline), and give `credentialExpiredEmail()` the same context treatment before its 1 Sep firing.

**Corrected template copy (draft):**
> **Subject:** Your {club} fob will expire on {date} unless you renew your membership
>
> Hi {firstName},
>
> Your fob (serial {serial}) is due to expire on **{date}**.
>
> Fob access is tied to your club membership. If you renew your membership for the coming season, your fob stays active — its expiry is extended automatically once your renewal is processed, and you do not need to do anything with the fob itself.
>
> **If you have already renewed your membership, you can ignore this email.** Your fob's expiry will be updated shortly.
>
> If you have not renewed yet, please renew your membership before {date} to keep your access.
>
> Any questions, just reply to this email.

**One-off correction email (draft, to recipients of the bare email):**
> **Subject:** About the fob expiry email — what it actually means
>
> Hi {firstName},
>
> In the last few days you received an automated email from AccessBuddy saying your fob is expiring soon. Sorry — it was missing the context, and understandably caused some confusion.
>
> Here is the full picture: your fob will expire on **1 September** only if your club membership has not been renewed for the new season. Renewing your membership keeps your fob active — once your renewal is processed, the fob's expiry is extended automatically and you do not need to do anything with the fob itself.
>
> **If you have already renewed your membership, there is nothing you need to do** — please ignore both this and the earlier email.
>
> If you have not renewed yet, please renew before 1 September to keep your access.
>
> Apologies again for the confusion. The wording of the automated email has been fixed so future reminders explain this properly.

**Send plan for the correction:** recipient list from the audit-log query (Appendix A) — the successful `credentialExpiryWarning` sends of the last 4 days; send as P2 through the new queue (or manually throttled under the daily budget after the Resend upgrade); once-off script, not a new scheduled job; every send audited with subject per email standards.

---

## Executive summary

The three reported issues are one incident with one root cause and one independent trigger.

On 1–2 August the 2am daily cron (`accessbuddy-daily-cron` → `/api/cron/daily`) sent 30-day fob-expiry warnings to the SMLSC seasonal cohort. Because the platform normalises season expiry to **1 September**, the entire active cohort (up to 354 credentials) qualified in a single run — far past Resend's free-tier cap of **100 emails/day**. Every send past the cap failed. The failure is swallowed in code (`sendEmail` logs, writes an `email_failed` audit row, returns void), so:

- **Issue 1 (login):** login is email-only (Firebase magic link in browser, 6-digit OTP in PWA). With the cap exhausted, auth emails fail silently while the UI says "we sent you a code". Members were logged out in the first place by the 14 July v1.11.0 deploy (`cd70131` rotated the session-signing key, invalidating all OTP/passkey sessions) and/or natural 14-day cookie expiry ~28 July. Logout was benign; the inability to log back in is the Resend cap.
- **Issue 2 (email limit):** sends past ~100/day failed silently; failed 30-day warnings are **permanently lost** (the warning fires only at exactly 30 days out; no dedupe/backfill). Two more cap-breaching spikes are already scheduled: **~25 Aug** (7-day warnings, same cohort) and **~1–2 Sep** (credential-expired blast).
- **Issue 3 (template):** the bare wording is the hardcoded code default — the per-tenant override system is dead configuration (the `email_configurations` table doesn't exist in prod; no send path reads it anyway). The cron also does **not** exclude members who already renewed (only fully reprogrammed-and-confirmed credentials are excluded), so renewed members legitimately got the warning — hence the confusion.

## Causal chain

```
Season expiry normalised to 1 Sep (route.ts:150)
  → whole cohort hits diffDays === 30 on the same day (1–2 Aug)
    → cron attempts up to ~354 sends in one run
      → Resend free tier caps at 100/day
        → sends 101+ fail; sendEmail swallows error (email.ts:224-249)
          → auth emails (magic link / OTP) also fail silently
            → members logged out by 14 Jul key rotation / cookie expiry cannot re-authenticate
```

Contributing factors: fire-and-forget send path (no queue, no retry, no daily budget); auth and bulk email share one unprioritised quota; template lacked business context since v1.0.0 (`f36375a`); override system unwired; no alerting on `email_failed` bursts.

**Evidence:** `apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:9,59-93` (fail-closed HMAC verification, 14-day TTL); `sign-in-form.tsx:75-97` (email-only paths); commit `cd70131`; agents' full traces.

1. Check the Resend dashboard for quota state; daily reset is midnight UTC = 10:00 AEST.

4. Code fix (with issue 2): propagate send failures for auth-critical templates so sign-in routes return an honest error instead of `{ sent: true }`.

**Verification:** member confirms login; `audit_log` shows no `email_failed` rows for `verificationCode`/`magicLink` after fix.

**Failure mode:** fire-and-forget; no retry, no queue; cron returns 200 even if every email failed; failed 30-day warnings never re-fire.

**Queue design (proposed):**
- New `email_queue` table (id, tenant, template, recipient, payload, priority, status, attempts, earliest_send_at, created_at, sent_at, error).
- **Priority classes:** P0 auth (magic link, OTP — sent inline, never queued, but counted); P1 transactional (payment, pickup, approval); P2 bulk (expiry warnings, summaries, correction blasts).

- **Drain:** cron (reuse `/api/cron/daily` or a new 15-min cron) drains queue oldest-first within priority, spreading the ~354-recipient cohort across ~4–5 days automatically.
- **Retry/backlog:** failed sends set `status='failed'` and re-queue with backoff (max 3 attempts); the currently-lost 30-day warnings get backfilled by enqueueing everyone from the failed-recipient query.
- **Cron change:** expiry-warning windows become ranges (e.g. 30–26 days and 7–3 days with sent-dedupe against `email_queue`/audit) so spreading over days doesn't skip anyone.

## Problem

Three linked production incidents at AccessBuddy (SMLSC tenant live): (1) a member reports being logged out and unable to log back in; (2) the Resend daily email limit (100/day free tier) was hit, so an unknown subset of outbound emails silently failed and future blasts risk the same; (3) a fob-expiry notification went out without the critical renewal context ("expires 1 Sep unless you renew; ignore if already renewed"), generating confused member queries. Nick needs evidence-backed diagnosis and a plan per issue before anything is changed.

## Vision

Nick opens one report and instantly sees what actually happened across all three issues — including whether the email limit caused the login failure — with a concrete, low-risk plan per issue he can approve line by line. Nothing has been touched; everything is ready to execute on approval.

## Out of Scope

No code changes, no deploys, no database writes, no emails sent, no template edits — this run is investigation and planning only. No redesign of the wider notification system beyond the queue needed for the daily limit. No Resend plan upgrade decision (surfaced as an option only).

## Constraints

- Read-only against production: SELECTs and API GETs only; no mutations.
- All agent work on the Fable model per Nick's explicit instruction.
- Email architecture facts from `context/facts.md` are authoritative (Resend, 27-event registry, `email_configurations` overrides, `setEmailBranding()` convention).
- Correction email and template copy must carry tenant branding and the renewal business context.
- Plans must respect the existing stack (Bun/Hono, Postgres/Drizzle, Cloud Run) — no new infrastructure unless unavoidable.

## Goal

Deliver a three-part incident report — login failure, email-limit audit with queued-send design (15/day reserved for auth), fob-expiry template fix with correction-email draft and recipient list — each with root cause evidence and an approval-ready action plan, with zero production mutations performed.

## Verdict on ISC-29

**The blast → limit → login chain is CONFIRMED as the re-authentication failure leg, but it is NOT the whole story.** The member's logout and the member's inability to log back in have *different* causes. The lockout required both legs to fire — classic Swiss cheese alignment.

## Fault Tree

```
TOP EVENT: Member locked out, no error surfaced to anyone
└── AND
    ├── LEG A — Session invalidated (why they were logged out)
    │   SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET rotated 14 July
    │   → verifyWebauthnSessionCookie() returns null for all pre-rotation cookies
    │     (code/apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:59-71 — signed cookie, no fallback, verify-or-null)
    │   → forced logout on next visit; no dual-key grace window, no user messaging
    │
    └── LEG B — Re-authentication email never arrived (why they couldn't get back in)
        Daily cron sweeps credentials expiring within 31 days and sends per-credential
        warnings in an unbounded loop (code/apps/web/src/app/api/cron/daily/route.ts:390-395)
        → blast consumed the Resend free-tier 100/day quota [per agent evidence]
        → subsequent sends fail at the provider; sendEmail() catches, writes an
          email_failed audit entry + console.error, and returns — no throw, no retry,
          no alert (code/apps/web/src/lib/services/email.ts:233-271)
        → magic-link route still returns { sent: true } to the member regardless
          (code/apps/web/src/app/api/auth/send-magic-link/route.ts:95)
        → member is told the link was sent; nothing arrives; repeat attempts burn
          further quota

AMPLIFIER (independent thread, worsened both legs):
        credential_expiry_warning default template
        (code/packages/shared/src/email-events.ts:387-400) lacks the renewal context
        ("expires 1 Sep unless you renew; ignore if already renewed")
        → confused members contact the club AND visit the app to check
        → drives stale-session members into Leg A, and their login attempts into Leg B
```

**Key causal insight:** the blast didn't just exhaust the quota — via the confusing template it *generated the traffic* of returning members with 14-July-invalidated sessions who then needed auth emails the exhausted quota couldn't deliver. The three issues are one system event, not three coincidences.

## Contributing Factors (classified)

**Proximate causes**
1. Fob-expiry blast exhausted the Resend 100/day cap (Leg B trigger).
2. Signing-key rotation on 14 July invalidated standing sessions (Leg A trigger — independent; would have caused only a silent re-login if Leg B hadn't fired).

**Latent conditions** (present long before, actionable)
3. **No budget/priority layer between event producers and Resend.** Transactional auth email and bulk notifications share one unprioritized pipe with a hard external cap. Any bulk event can starve auth. (Fix = queue design, ISC-14..19, with the 15/day auth reserve.)

**Full report:** `~/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/artifacts/reviews/2026-08-01-incident-report-email-cap-login-template.md` (interim — provisional root cause; final confirmation needs the send logs). Condensed version:

**The finding: your three issues are one incident.** Season expiry is normalised to 1 September, so on 1–2 August the whole SMLSC cohort hit "exactly 30 days out" together and the 2am cron tried to email all of them (upper bound 354) through Resend's 100/day free tier. Everything past the cap failed — and `sendEmail` swallows failures (logs an `email_failed` audit row, returns void), so nothing surfaced. Login is email-only (magic link/OTP), so locked-out members' sign-in emails died silently while the UI said "check your email". The logout itself was the 14 July deploy rotating the session-signing key (plus natural 14-day cookie expiry ~28 July) — harmless alone, a lockout only in combination. The bare template amplified it: confused members flooded back to the app with dead sessions, burning more quota.

**Issue 1 — member can't log in. Plan:**
1. Resend dashboard now: confirm quota; daily reset is 10:00 AEST. Then member retries "Resend code".
2. If they have a passkey enrolled, Face ID login works right now (no email).
3. Fallback: generate a Firebase sign-in link via Admin SDK, send from your mailbox (your call).
4. Fix (with issue 2): sign-in routes must return an honest error when the send fails, not `{ sent: true }`.

**Issue 2 — sent vs unsent, and the queue. Plan:**
- Counts are fully recoverable from the `audit_log` (`email_sent`/`email_failed` rows carry recipient, subject, template, error) — but this box can't reach prod: no `gcloud` (Linux or Mac), DB is private-IP, both Resend keys are send-only. **Fastest path: Resend dashboard. Authoritative: install gcloud + cloud-sql-proxy, run the four prepared queries in Appendix A** (sent/failed breakdown, failed-recipient list, correction recipient list, cohort sizing).
- Failed 30-day warnings are permanently lost (exact-day check, no backfill) — the backlog needs re-queuing once we have the list.
- **Queue design:** `email_queue` table; P0 auth / P1 transactional / P2 bulk; 85/day budget (100 − 15 reserved for login); drain oldest-first within priority, spreading the cohort over ~4–5 days; failed sends retry with backoff; alert on any `email_failed`.
- **Recommendation: also upgrade to Resend Pro (~US$20/mo) today** — two more cap-breaching spikes are already scheduled (~25 Aug 7-day warnings, 1–2 Sep expired-credential blast) and renewal-season traffic collides with them. Order matters: make failures loud first — quota alone treats the symptom.

**Issue 3 — template + correction. Plan:**
- What went out was the hardcoded default (unchanged since v1.0.0): "ACTION REQUIRED: Your credential is expiring soon… Please take action to renew it." The tenant-override system is dead config — the table doesn't exist in prod and no send path reads it. And the cron doesn't skip renewed-but-not-reprogrammed members, so renewed people got it too — your inbox was the detection system.
- **Fix:** edit `credentialExpiryWarningEmail()` + subject, ship as `fix:` (deploys via release-please). Bundle: skip credentials with `pendingExpiresAt` set, and fix `credentialExpiredEmail` before it fires on 1 Sep. New copy drafted in the report ("Your {club} fob will expire on {date} unless you renew your membership… If you have already renewed, you can ignore this email.").
- **Correction email:** drafted in the report. Guards: recipients strictly from the audit log (never inferred), exclude anyone who renewed since the blast, idempotent once-off script. List comes to you for sign-off before anything sends.

**Suggested sequence:** (1) Resend dashboard + Pro upgrade + unblock the member today; (2) one `fix:` release — template fix, renewed-member skip, honest auth errors, failure alert; (3) run Appendix A queries → backfill lost warnings → correction email after your sign-off on the list; (4) build the queue; (5) follow-ups (migration 0010, wire the override system, `expiryDate`/`expiresAt` mismatch).

🖊️ STORY:
- Three separate complaints hid one compounding production incident
- Fable agents traced blast, cap, and silent failures
- Root cause: two faults aligned, template amplified both
- Plans ready; your approval gates every next step

content.text:
Important new evidence — and it partially changes the Issue 1 diagnosis. If the member is *receiving* the magic-link email and clicking it, then for them this isn't quota starvation at all: the email got through, but the **callback is failing to establish a session** and bouncing them back to the start. That's a third fault, distinct from both legs we identified.

Two prime suspects from what we already know: the classic Firebase email-link cross-device trap (the email address is stashed in the requesting browser's localStorage — open the link in a different browser or an in-app mail viewer and there's no stored email, so the app asks for it again; if that page *restarts* the flow instead of completing it, you get exactly this infinite loop), and the 14 July `cd70131` commit — "remove Host-header trust" could have changed how the emailed link URL or the session cookie is derived, making the cookie silently fail to set. Launching a focused Fable agent to trace the callback path and the diff.

input.description: Trace magic-link redirect loop
input.prompt:
READ-ONLY INVESTIGATION — modify nothing, send nothing, no DB writes. Evidence with file:line citations.

Context: AccessBuddy repo at ~/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/code (Next.js App Router + Bun/Hono, Firebase Auth). Prod runs main @ v1.10.2 (commit 288ac64-ish); the local checkout is branch fix/tenant-2-readiness which INCLUDES unreleased commits — always distinguish what main/prod runs (use `git show main:<path>` or `git diff main...HEAD -- <path>`) from what the branch has. Wait — first verify which of the 2026-07-14 commits (e.g. cd70131 "fix(auth): remove Host-header trust and fail closed on session signing", a960eba "fix(auth): move OTP store and rate limiting to Postgres") are on main vs only on the branch, and whether v1.11.0 (tag exists on origin) contains them; that determines what prod actually runs.

BUG REPORT (live member, SMLSC tenant, prod https://accessbuddy.com.au): they request a sign-in email, receive it, click the magic link, and are sent BACK to the enter-your-email page — stuck in an infinite loop. They never get a session.

Known flow (from prior investigation): browser sign-in posts to /api/auth/send-magic-link; apps/web/src/lib/services/magic-link.ts calls adminAuth.generateSignInWithEmailLink(email, actionCodeSettings) and emails the link; the callback should call Firebase client signInWithEmailLink then POST the ID token to /api/auth/session (apps/web/src/app/api/auth/session/route.ts) to mint a 14-day Firebase session cookie.

Investigate and answer:
1. THE CALLBACK: find the page the emailed link lands on (actionCodeSettings.url in magic-link.ts — quote it and how the base URL is derived). Trace the client code on that page: isSignInWithEmailLink check, where it reads the email (localStorage key?), what happens when the stored email is MISSING (cross-device / different browser / in-app mail viewer case): does it prompt for the email and complete signInWithEmailLink(email, link), or does it redirect to the sign-in page — and would the sign-in page then just send a NEW link (the loop)?
2. FAILURE BRANCHES that redirect back to sign-in: expired link (Firebase links are one-time/short-lived), already-used link (mail-client link prefetching can consume it!), auth/invalid-action-code handling, POST /api/auth/session failure (what does the client do on non-200?), cookie set but immediately rejected (inspect cookie attributes: secure, sameSite, domain, name; middleware that validates the session and redirects to sign-in — quote the middleware matcher and its redirect).
3. THE 14 JULY CHANGE: show the diff of cd70131 (and anything else touching auth/session/middleware since v1.10.2) as it affects (a) how the emailed link's base URL/origin is derived (Host-header removal → env-derived URL? mismatch with the LB domain?), (b) session cookie verification in middleware — could a pre-existing Firebase session cookie now fail verification and force sign-in redirect even AFTER a successful callback? Distinguish: is this change live in prod (on main / in v1.11.0) or not?
4. Rank the candidate causes for the observed loop (received email → click → back to email entry) with likelihood, stating which are testable without sending email (e.g. curl the callback URL shape, inspect middleware redirect) and run any safe read-only probes (curl -I https://accessbuddy.com.au/... to observe redirects/cookie headers — GET requests fine, DO NOT trigger sends).
5. For each ranked cause, the minimal fix and how the member could be unblocked TODAY without a deploy (e.g. open link in same browser that requested it, copy link URL into the original browser, use OTP path via PWA, passkey).

Return: PROD-VS-BRANCH (which commits live), CALLBACK-TRACE, FAILURE-BRANCHES, JULY14-DIFF-IMPACT, LIVE-PROBES (curl evidence), RANKED-CAUSES, UNBLOCK-TODAY, MINIMAL-FIXES. Mark anything unverifiable as UNVERIFIED. No fabrication.

content.text:
The trace agent is running. While it works, two questions for the member would discriminate between the top suspects fast — worth asking if you're already in contact:

1. **Are they clicking the link on the same device and browser they typed their email into?** The Firebase email-link flow stores the address in the requesting browser's localStorage — opening the link in a different browser, another device, or a mail app's built-in viewer breaks that, and a mishandled "confirm your email" fallback produces exactly this loop.
2. **What email service are they on — Outlook/Hotmail or corporate mail?** Microsoft SafeLinks and similar scanners prefetch links, and Firebase magic links are one-time use. If a scanner consumes the link before the human clicks it, every real click arrives already-invalid and bounces to the start.

I'll report the ranked diagnosis, a same-day unblock for the member, and the minimal fix once the agent returns.

- **Link URL:** `apps/web/src/lib/services/magic-link.ts:28-31` — `const appUrl = clientEnv.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL;` then `url: \`${appUrl}/auth/callback?redirect=${encodeURIComponent(redirect)}\``. Env-derived (GitHub secret build-arg, `deploy.yml:64`; runtime `infra/terraform/main.tf:312`), **not** Host-header derived. Line 27 forces `sendEmails: true` (magic-link emails bypass the tenant flag). The emailed link points first at the Firebase handler on `accessbuddy-prod.firebaseapp.com` (authDomain verified baked into the live bundle, below) which forwards to the callback with `oobCode`/`mode` appended.
- **Callback client** (`apps/web/src/app/auth/callback/auth-callback.tsx`):

  - :24 reads **`localStorage.getItem("emailForSignIn")`** — set by `apps/web/src/app/sign-in/sign-in-form.tsx:95` as `email.trim()` (**not lowercased**; the send route lowercases at `send-magic-link/route.ts:21` before generating the link — see cause 4).
  - :26 **missing email → `window.prompt("Please enter your email to confirm sign-in:")`** — a JS prompt, not a page. Cancel/blocked prompt → :28 "Email required to complete sign-in." error card with a **"Back to sign-in" link** (:93-94). It does NOT auto-redirect, but the only exit is the sign-in page, which sends a NEW link — that is the human loop.
  - :33 `signInWithEmailLink` → :38-44 POST `/api/auth/session`; non-200 throws → :80 generic "Sign-in failed. The link may have expired." + Back to sign-in.

| Branch | Behaviour | Loop shape |
|---|---|---|
| `isSignInWithEmailLink` false | error card (:20) | manual (click Back) |
| expired/used oobCode (`auth/invalid-action-code`) | caught at :79-81, generic error | manual |
| wrong/mismatched email in prompt | same catch, same generic error | manual |
| session POST non-200 (route returns 401 on any failure, `session/route.ts:128`) | same catch | manual |

Cookie attributes (`session/route.ts:32-38`): name `session`, `httpOnly`, `secure` (prod), `sameSite: "lax"`, `path: "/"`, no `domain` (host-only), 14-day maxAge. Middleware (`middleware.ts:7,13`) exempts `/sign-in` and `/auth/callback`; it only checks cookie **presence**, verification happens in server components via `getAuthUser`.

**Not live in prod, and not on this code path even on the branch.** cd70131 touches `verify-otp`, `webauthn/login`, `dev-login`, `env.ts`, `lib/auth.ts` (webauthn HMAC → dedicated `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET`, fail-closed), and terraform — it does **not** touch `magic-link.ts`, the callback, `session/route.ts`, or `middleware.ts`. (a) Link base URL was already env-derived on main; the Host-header trust removed was dev-login gating, not URL derivation. (b) It changes verification only for `webauthn.`-prefixed cookies (OTP/passkey sessions), not Firebase magic-link session cookies — and since it is NOT deployed, it cannot have broken a pre-existing cookie. If it ever ships, existing OTP/passkey sessions signed with `CRON_SECRET ?? 1. **Cross-device / in-app mail browser open (HIGH).** Link opened in the Gmail/Outlook in-app viewer or a different browser than the one that requested it → no `emailForSignIn` in that context's localStorage → `window.prompt` (:26). **Diagnosis of the loop (report updated at `artifacts/reviews/2026-08-01-incident-report-email-cap-login-template.md`):**

Since the member receives and clicks the email, quota starvation isn't what's blocking *them*. The callback flow has a fragile fallback, and the most likely cause (HIGH confidence) is the **cross-device trap**: the app stores the typed email in the requesting browser's localStorage; when the link opens in a different browser or the mail app's built-in viewer, that's absent and the callback falls back to a bare `window.prompt` — which many in-app viewers silently suppress. Result: error card → "Back to sign-in" → new link → loop, exactly as described. Runner-up causes: clicking older one-time links from the pile of sign-in emails (self-reinforcing once looping), the browser discarding the session cookie (this silent-bounce leg was live-verified against prod), and a genuine wrinkle worth fixing regardless — the send route lowercases the email but localStorage keeps the typed case.

**Correction to yesterday's report — being upfront:** I attributed the logout to the 14 July signing-key rotation. That was wrong. The agent proved those commits are **branch-only, never deployed** — prod v1.11.0 differs from v1.10.2 by landing-page copy alone (verified via git ancestry and probing the live bundle). 1. In the email, long-press/right-click the sign-in button → **Copy link** → paste it into the **same browser where you typed your email**.
2. Use only the **newest** sign-in email; delete the older ones.
3. If asked for your email, type it in **all lowercase**, no spaces.
4. Use a normal (not private) window with cookies enabled.

## Problem

The v0.7 pack (OneDrive 00_Inbox, 9 Jul 2026) cannot be read linearly — Nick jumps around when explaining it. One correction to what I told you earlier from the agent's stale view: `fix/tenant-2-readiness` **is pushed** (remote head matches local `e923f4c`), so that's the branch behind your other thread and its PR — the commit trail there ("fix(ci): pass DATABASE_URL…", "three defects surfaced by the DB-backed tests' first real CI run", latest "fix teardown FK order") is a live fight to get CI green. ═══ PAI ═══════════════════════════
🔄 ITERATION on: consolidating incident thread, tenant-2 thread, and repo branch state
📃 CONTENT:

**Where everything stands**

**Deployed:** prod = v1.11.0 (`865a600`) — that's v1.10.2 plus landing copy only. None of the auth/DB hardening is live yet. Local `main` is 4 commits behind origin (just a fast-forward); working tree clean.

**Stream 1 — this thread (incident triage):**
- Issue 1 (login) closed — user error; five callback-hardening fixes remain as recommended UX debt.
- Sent/failed audit + correction-email recipient list: **blocked solely on you** — temp full-access Resend key (script ready), the dashboard, or gcloud+cloud-sql-proxy. Time-sensitive: Resend free-tier log retention, and failed 30-day warnings are otherwise unrecoverable except via the prod `audit_log`.
- Drafted and awaiting your approval: corrected fob-expiry template, one-off correction email (guarded), queue design (85/day budget, 15 reserved for auth), Resend Pro recommendation. Hard dates: **~25 Aug** 7-day-warning spike, **1–2 Sep** expired-credential blast — both breach 100/day again if nothing changes.

**Stream 2 — other thread (`fix/tenant-2-readiness`, 10 commits, pushed, PR checks being iterated):**
- Contents: auth hardening (dedicated session-signing secret, Host-header trust removed), Postgres OTP store (fixes the flaky PWA OTP on scale-to-zero), tenant isolation + RLS binding, migration-baseline repair + **migration 0010 (finally creates `email_configurations` in prod)**, error boundaries, and first-ever DB-backed tests in CI — the last four commits are all about getting those tests passing. The incident `fix:` release and tenant-2 touch the same auth surface (`auth.ts`, sign-in/OTP routes; callback hardening touches `sign-in-form.tsx`). My recommendation on sequencing: **ship the incident hotfix small and first** — branch off `origin/main` with only template + subject, skip-renewals (`pendingExpiresAt`), expired-email context, honest auth-send errors, `email_failed` alert. It's low-risk, reviewable in minutes, and beats the 25 Aug deadline independently of the CI fight. Fold the **callback hardening into tenant-2** instead (same files, avoids conflicts). **Housekeeping (low priority):** ~15 stale feat/fix branches on the remote look merged (reconciliation series, mobile-nav, etc.) — worth a prune pass sometime; local `main` needs a fast-forward.

READ-ONLY INVESTIGATION — modify nothing, no DB writes, no emails. File:line evidence. Repo: ~/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/code. BUG REPORT (SMLSC tenant, prod): Nick Vouk submitted a DEACTIVATION request for fob serial 3001. The admin requests view now shows it in BOTH "awaiting programming" AND "awaiting pickup". A deactivation should have nothing to pick up.

Investigate:
1. Map the request state machine for deactivation requests (packages/shared/src/state-machine.ts, request pipeline services, request types/enums). What states should a deactivation pass through? Is "awaiting pickup" ever legitimate for a deactivation?
2. How do the admin queue sections compute membership ("awaiting programming" / "awaiting pickup" groupings — the admin requests page is a server component with grouped status sections)? Could ONE request appear in two sections, or must this be TWO rows (e.g. the deactivation request + an auto-created paired/replacement request)?
3. Paired-replacement suspicion: recent branch fix/orphan-link-creates-paired-replacement exists, and a commit "chore: run paired-replacement backfill on container start" (85d89b0). Read that branch's diff and the backfill logic: does prod contain the backfill or the bug it fixes? Could a deactivation (or the backfill) have spawned a spurious replacement/pickup row for 3001? Establish whether that branch is merged into origin/main (git merge-base / branch --contains).
4. Determine the most likely cause with evidence, state whether the fix is (a) a data correction for this one request (write the exact read-only diagnostic SQL to confirm, plus the corrective SQL Nick could review — DO NOT run any write), (b) a code fix (name file/function and the minimal change), or both.
5. Note any similar latent cases the diagnostic SQL would also surface (other deactivations with paired pickup rows).

input.description: Investigate expiry date mismatch
input.prompt:
READ-ONLY INVESTIGATION — modify nothing, no DB writes, no emails. File:line evidence. Repo: ~/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/code. IMPORTANT: prod runs origin/main @ 865a600 (v1.11.0) — analyse prod behaviour via `git show 865a600:<path>`, NOT the checked-out fix/tenant-2-readiness branch; note branch differences separately.

BUG REPORT (SMLSC tenant, prod): on attestation renewal requests the UI shows BOTH:
  "Renewal attestation (2026/2027) - update expiry to 2027-08-31"
  "Staged new expiry: 1 Sept 2027"
  "Requested 21 July 2026, 05:42 pm"
Why does one line say 31 August and the other 1 September for the same staged expiry?

Investigate:
1. Find where the attestation renewal computes the new expiry (likely `new Date(year, 8, 1)` style — season end 1 September, cf. api/cron/daily/route.ts:150 and the attestation completion route apps/web/src/app/api/v1/t/[slug]/attestations/[token]/route.ts staging pendingExpiresAt). Quote the computation and what exact timestamp gets stored (with timezone semantics — is it midnight LOCAL (AEST) or UTC?).
2. Find the TWO render sites: (a) the "update expiry to 2027-08-31" label (likely a request/audit description string built with toISOString().slice(0,10) or date-fns format in UTC), (b) the "Staged new expiry: 1 Sept 2027" display (likely formatted with en-AU locale in local time). Quote both formatting calls. Confirm the off-by-one is a timezone rendering artefact: 2027-09-01T00:00+10:00 == 2027-08-31T14:00Z → UTC date-only = 2027-08-31.
3. Determine which value is AUTHORITATIVE for behaviour: what does the credential's expiresAt become after confirm-programming promotes pendingExpiresAt, what does the daily cron compare against (diffDays logic), and what gets shown to members/programmers/Integriti? Is there any REAL early-expiry risk (fob dying 31 Aug instead of 1 Sep), or is it purely display? Check whether expiry comparisons use UTC or local (cron runs 2am AEST).
4. Sweep for the same date-only-UTC formatting mistake elsewhere (grep toISOString().slice / .split("T")[0] / format patterns on expiry fields) — list other affected surfaces (emails, tables, audit labels).
5. Propose the minimal fix: single formatting helper (en-AU, Australia/Melbourne) for date-only display of expiry timestamps, and/or storing date-only; note migration implications if any.

Return: COMPUTATION (stored value + tz semantics), RENDER-SITES (both, quoted), AUTHORITATIVE-VALUE & REAL-RISK (early expiry yes/no with evidence), OTHER-AFFECTED-SURFACES, MINIMAL-FIX. Mark unverifiable items UNVERIFIED. No fabrication.
